$comment: Residual cause census for the committed ACTIVITY oracle corpus (activity-oracle-harness / T6), measured AFTER T5 routed renderActivity through the klimt document shell (D6). Sibling of oracle/goldens/svg-sequence/diff-census.json, but a DIFFERENT shape: sequence's census sorts every Diff into six fixed buckets; this one ranks the remaining diff PATHS by the weight they carry, because T6's brief asks for a work queue ordered by where the residual actually lives, not a bucket tally. Every number here is a pure function of the committed corpus at measuredAgainstCommit: each of the 268 status:"baseline" fixtures in diff-baseline.json is rendered through tests/oracle/svg-conformance/render-fixture-activity.ts#renderFixtureActivity with a DeterministicMeasurer and tests/helpers/fixture-include-store.ts#fixtureIncludeStore() -- the identical seams activity.diff-baseline.ratchet.test.ts uses -- and compared with compareSvg(ours, golden, 'deterministic') (tests/oracle/svg-conformance/compare.ts). Paths are normalised by replacing every positional index with [], so svg/g[1]/rect[3]/@x and svg/g[1]/rect[7]/@x are one family. RANKED BY WEIGHT, NOT COUNT (D2): compareSvg short-circuits on node-type, tag and child-count mismatch and charges each an upper bound on what descending could have cost, so a [childCount] diff standing for a whole skipped subtree carries far more weight than the single record it contributes to diffCount. Ranking by occurrence would put svg/@viewBox[] (527 records, 0.5% of the residual weight) above svg/g[][childCount] (209 records, 91.6%) and point the next mission at the wrong work. status "error" (82) and "jar-error" (23) fixtures contribute NOTHING here -- an unrenderable fixture and a jar error page both have no meaningful diff set and must never read as zero (D8, D12).

descent.note: The mission headline. Before = T2's pre-chrome pin (oracle/goldens/svg-activity/diff-baseline.json at commit 9524864f); after = this measurement. Same 268 fixtures, same seams, same comparator; the only change between them is T5. diffCount rising on 57 fixtures beside a weightedScore that fell on all 268 is the artefact D2 predicted in advance: collapsing the 12-marker defs short-circuit converts an unexamined 'cost 1' into a real per-attribute comparison.

geometryResidual.note: width/height/viewBox go BOTH WAYS and no constant margin explains them. viewBox[2]/viewBox[3] are byte-identical to width/height on our side for all 268 fixtures (verified: zero mismatches), so they are the same measurement reported twice and are not listed separately per fixture. Worked examples the T6 brief names: numalo-91-pole243 is 52 wide against the jar's 64 (NARROWER); darote-51-kuta407 is 144 against 129 (WIDER). Every width differs; 9 of 268 heights already match.

childCountResidual.note: THE SINGLE LARGEST ITEM: svg/g[][childCount] carries 91.6% of the remaining weight. This is MISSING INK, not chrome -- our root group holds fewer drawn children than the jar's on 190 of 268 fixtures, i.e. unported activity content. D13 measured the PRE-T5 split as 168 fewer / 20 equal / 80 more (55 at exactly +2, the two background rects). T5 removed those rects, which is why the +2 cohort collapsed (80 more -> 19, only 9 still at +2) and the equal cohort grew (20 -> 59); the 20 that were equal only because two chrome rects masked a two-element deficit now show -2, exactly as D13 predicted, and their weightedScore still FELL. A childCount mismatch short-circuits the whole subtree, so closing this gap is worth more than every attribute family below it combined.

namedFamilies.finding: We resolve theme.colors.background to #FFFFFF where the jar resolves #1B1B1B, so the root style/background carries the wrong colour AND the background rect the jar paints under its own paintBackcolor guard (SvgGraphics.java:186-192) is correctly declined on our resolved white. The guard is faithful; its INPUT is wrong. Found by T5 while verifying the guard, handed to this census.
namedFamilies.correction: The T5 decision-journal entry names velodu-59-sada437 as a second instance of this family. It is NOT one: that fixture's golden is the jar's OWN graphical error page (green-on-black, PSystemError styling), it is pinned status:"jar-error" in diff-baseline.json, and it contributes no number to this census at all. Its #000000 background is the error page's, not a resolved theme. Verified at T6, not inherited. skinparam mode dark occurs on exactly ONE fixture in the whole 373-fixture corpus.

namedFamilies.finding: The only surviving root-attribute VALUE diff besides background. Source sets `skinparam preserveAspectRatio xMinYMid slice`; the jar emits that verbatim on the root, we emit the hardcoded default `none`. Not a missing attribute -- the document shell emits all 7 root attributes on all 268 fixtures (verified) -- an unported skinparam.

The only surviving svg/defs[1][childCount] diff, and the opposite of the pre-mission one: OUR defs is empty (0) and the JAR's holds 1 child. Source is `skinparam activity { BackgroundColor red-green }`; the jar expands the two-colour form into a <linearGradient> in defs and fills the rect with url(#...). We emit no gradient. Confirms the D6 change was right in general -- 267 of 268 goldens have an EMPTY defs, matching ours -- and isolates the one shape that needs it.
